notes.meaning: God commands the prophet to cry out with all his might, like a loud ram's horn, without holding anything back. He must clearly point out the rebellion and sins of God's people so they cannot ignore their wrongdoing. A messenger of God cannot speak soft, comforting words when serious sin needs to be exposed.

On the outside, the people looked very religious because they attended worship every day and asked God for guidance. They acted like a faithful nation eager for God to draw near and give just rulings. Yet this devotion was only a show, because their hearts did not truly obey God's commands in everyday life.

The people complained to God that He was ignoring their religious fasts and not rewarding their self-denial. God answered that while they were skipping meals, they were still pursuing their own business and pleasures. At the very same time, they were being harsh and demanding toward their laborers.

Instead of producing humility, their fasts led to bitter arguments, quarreling, and even physical violence. Going without food without a changed heart only made them angry and irritable toward others. God tells them that such bitter behavior will keep their prayers from ever being heard in heaven.

God asks if a true fast is merely bowing one's head like a bent reed and lying in rough sackcloth and ashes for a day. These gloomy outward gestures mean nothing to Him if they are done only for show. God is not pleased with an empty ceremony that leaves the heart unchanged.

The fast God really wants is the removal of injustice and the release of those who are treated unfairly. It means cancelling unfair debts, stopping extortion, and freeing people trapped in cruel bondage. True self-denial begins when we stop harming others and break every heavy burden weighing them down.

differ.view: Some hold that the prophet is setting aside physical fasting altogether to replace it with works of mercy.
Physical fasting remains a valuable duty, but going without food is incomplete unless it leads directly to active justice and charity.

notes.meaning: An acceptable fast includes giving food to the hungry and opening one's home to the homeless. It means providing clothing to those who have none and not turning away from relatives or fellow human beings in need. When we see someone hurting, we are looking at our own flesh and blood.

When God's people show genuine mercy to the needy, their darkness will quickly turn into the bright light of dawn. God will heal their old wounds and restore their well-being. Their upright living will march before them like a guide, while God's own glory protects them from behind.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular teachers emphasize that social justice must flow directly from biblical worship and personal holiness rather than secular political movements.

notes.meaning: If people turn away from cruelty, God will gladly answer their prayers and declare that He is right beside them to help. But to enjoy this close fellowship, they must stop oppressing others. They must also put an end to pointing the finger in contempt and speaking harmful, deceitful words.

Believers are called to pour out their hearts and food to those who are suffering and in deep need. When people give of themselves with real compassion, their gloom will turn to sunshine. Even their darkest moments of sorrow will become as bright as the midday sun.

The Lord promises to guide His people faithfully, just as a shepherd leads his flock. Even during dry and difficult times, He will satisfy their souls and renew their physical strength. They will become like a lush, well-watered garden, fed by a cool spring whose waters never run dry.

God's people will rebuild the towns and walls that have lain in ruins for generations. They will restore the ancient foundations and repair the broken places in the city defenses. Because of this blessing, they will be remembered as peacemakers who made ruined streets safe and fit to live in once again.

God asks His people to treat the Sabbath—His holy day of rest—as holy ground by keeping their feet from selfish pursuits. They are to honor the day instead of filling it with their own business, worldly pleasures, or idle chatter. When kept in the right spirit, the Sabbath becomes a joyful delight rather than a heavy burden.

differ.view: Believers are morally bound to set apart the entire Christian Sabbath from secular business, worldly amusements, and idle words as a holy delight to God.
The Sabbath law was fulfilled in Christ, leaving New Testament believers free regarding the observance of specific holy days.

notes.meaning: When people honor God's holy day, they will find their greatest joy and satisfaction in the Lord Himself. God will lift them high above every danger, giving them victory and security in the land. He will fulfill every promise of blessing made long ago to their forefather Jacob, for the Lord's own mouth has promised it.
